status_note: fixed upstream in 30.30.0 by PR [#8840](https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot/pull/8840) ("parse ~ as a partial regex match from DuckDB 2.0"): `'abc' ~ 'b'` reads as `REGEXP_MATCHES` on 30.30.0.
summary: In the DuckDB dialect, the operator `~` reads as `RegexpFullMatch`, which writes `REGEXP_FULL_MATCH(s, p)`. DuckDB 2.0's `~` matches anywhere in the string, as `regexp_matches` does (its setting `regex_match_operator_semantics` chooses), so `'abc' ~ 'b'` is true in DuckDB and false as SQLGlot reads it. `!~` likewise.
repro: observed: `["SELECT REGEXP_FULL_MATCH('abc', 'b')"]`; DuckDB 2.0.0 gives `SELECT 'abc' ~ 'b'` as `true` and `SELECT regexp_full_match('abc', 'b')` as `false`.
handling: The SQL lift refuses `~` and `!~` between two operands, from the tokens, before parsing (`_check_regex_operators`); `regexp_matches` and `regexp_full_match` written as functions lift (#808).
found_by: the replay of DuckDB's sqllogictests (`function/string/regex_operators.test` L11, `test_similar_to.test` L87) through `sverify_dev.slt`, on #894

checked.note: triage: repro run on 30.30.0; tobymao/sqlglot searched
